browser: Claude Code in-app browser (Chromium) with direct QA injection

runtimeValidation.method: npm run qa:prepare fetched the stable 2.13.8 artifact together with both SHA-256-pinned startup files from the production origin and combined them into one payload; the payload was carried into a real Luogu tab through window.name (the page's meta CSP allows 'unsafe-eval' but blocks every cross-origin script and fetch, so the CDN cannot be reached from the page itself) and evaluated in the main world

startupMeasurement.method: Measured synchronous execution of the prepared 2.13.8 QA payload in the browser main world
startupMeasurement.purpose: Bootstrap execution budget; network integrity and delivery were independently verified by the production CDN gate and by re-hashing both pinned startup files fetched from the origin

productionCdn.priorReleaseStillByteIntact: 2.13.7 runtime re-fetched and re-hashed to ec4bca98c60ae3f6…, so installed 2.13.7 users keep passing their @require integrity check

hiddenIntroRouteScope.user: /user/52918 (introduction present in the Lentille payload, not rendered by Luogu)
hiddenIntroRouteScope.spaRoundTrips: home -> activity -> home -> article -> practice -> home -> following -> follower -> home, driven by real tab clicks and real anchor clicks; the introduction reappeared on every return to the home tab and never appeared on a sub-page
hiddenIntroRouteScope.directSubPageLoad: /user/52918/practice loaded directly: no introduction, no fallback card, feature stayed inert until the home tab was entered

settingsEntry.note: SELECTORS.navContainers only matches nav.lfe-body and nav.sidebar. When Luogu's left sidebar is in its unpinned drawer state the nav element carries neither class, so the 插件设置 entry is not injected. Identical in 2.13.7; not introduced by this release.

console.summary: No LuoguSP or luogusp.round1.cc error was observed on the exercised routes. The one site error, [@lfe/utils/error-handler] ApiResponseError Error: 用户尚未登录, is Luogu's own signed-out API response.

limitations: The in-app browser does not install Tampermonkey; the exact two pinned production startup files and the stable artifact were injected after the initial document load, so document-start restricted-page coverage was not repeated.

The browser pane was not displayed, so the page never composited: requestAnimationFrame had to be shimmed onto timers for the lifecycle remount to run, and screenshots were unavailable. All findings are DOM and computed-style assertions rather than images.
The browser session was not signed in, so IDE batch execution and private-message Ctrl+Click were not available.
Restricted article and paste recovery were not re-exercised in this behaviour-only release; their behaviour remains covered by the passing automated suite and the previous stable browser run.
